full_judgment:
2. The petitioner's case in short is that the plaintiff-opposite-parties instituted Title Suit No. 288 of 1976 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Dhaka which was subsequently transferred to the Assistant judge, Savar, Dhaka and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 372 of 1984 for a declaration of title in the suit properties wherein the defendant petitioner was added subsequently. The further case of the petitioner is that the plaintiff instituted the suit alleging that 4.48 acres of land of plot No. 148 of Touzi No. 8173 of mouza Salia under Police Station Savar, District Dhaka originally belonged to the Dhaka Nowab Estate out of which 3.79 acres of land was given in settlement by the Manager of the said Estate under his memo. No. 591 DG 15-8-51 to one Abdur Rashid Bepari son of Abdul Jabbar Fakir of Miton and on receipt of Salami granted receipt on 6-3-58. Said Abdur Rashid Bepari possessed and enjoyed the said land and paid rent to the Nowab Estate upto 1361 BS and during the settlement operation the land was recorded in the name of said Abdur Rashid Bepari at PRR stage. But it was omitted in the copy prepared under section 46 of Estate Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such objection raised in case No. 73 of 1964 and subsequently the land was recorded in the name of Abdur Rashid Bepari by opening khatian No. 38 who duly paid rent and got DCR. It is also the case, of the plaintiff that the name of said Abdur Rashid Bepari was recorded in the present RS khatian. Thereafter Abdur Rashid Bepari sold the suit properties to different persons including plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2. Plaintiff No. 2 transferred 76 decimals of land to the plaintiff No. 3 out of his purchased 95 decimals and plaintiff No. 4 purchased 1.89 decimals of land from other transferee of Abdur Rashid Bepari. Thereafter when the plaintiffs applied for mutation of their names in the RS khatian they found the name of Saidur Rahman already mutated in the khatian. The plaintiffs then filed Misc. Case No. 34 of 1975 before the defendant No. 1 who found that the Circle Officer (Rev) was not the competent authority to record the name of predecessor of Abdur Rashid Bepari and mutation of Saidur Rahman's name was also found illegal and order passed for cancellation of the name of Abdur Rashid Bepari and treated the suit properties as government khas land and that compelled the plaintiffs to file the present suit for declaration that the orders of the defendant No. 1 dated 6-8-1987 are illegal, null and void and the plaintiffs are the lawful owners of the suit property. 

 3. Defendant-opposite party No. 5 and the present defendant-petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement. It is the case of the present petitioner that the land comprising an area of 12.18 acres in plot No. 148 khatian 31/35, 93/31 (ka) Mouza Chalia JL No. 626 in Upazila Savar belonged to Dhaka Nawab Estabe and the land was given in settlement by the then Manager of the said Estate on 15-8-51 in favour of Abdus Samad, Abdur Rahman, Abdur Rashid who paid rent to the Nowab Estate Dhaka and they were recognized tenants and while Abdur Rahman and Abdur Rashid were possessing the land they sold 5.72 acres of land in plot No. 148 to Shahidur Rahman who mutated his name in the SA khatian in Misc. Case No. 5(b) of 73-74 for 5.72 acres. The name of Shahidur Rahman was also recorded in the RS Khatian. Thereafter Saidur Rahman sold 4.09 acres to the present petitioner by different registered kabalas and handed over the transferred land to the petitioner who thereafter mutated their names in the relevant SA Record of Right in Misc. Case No. 674(B)P-1/75-76 and paid rent and they developed the entire land and allotted the same to the members of the society. It is also the case of the present petitioner that during RS operation the plaintiff opposite parties filed Misc. Case No. 34.75 before the ADC (Rev.) Dhaka praying for mutation of their name in place of Sahidur Rahman which was ultimately rejected. The plaintiff opposite parties have no right title, and possession in the suit property and their kabalas were created with ulterior motive. 

 9. From the perusal of the papers filed it appears that the plaintiff filed the suit praying for a declaration that the plaintiffs are the rightful owners of the schedule property and that the orders passed by the defendant No. 1 on 6-8-76 is null and void and that the name of the plaintiff should be recorded in the present RS khatian in respect of the schedule of land showing 0.95 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff No. 1, 0.18 in favour of plaintiff No. 2, 0.76 in favour of plaintiff No. 3 and 1.90 in favour of plaintiff No. 4 after releasing it from the khas khatian of the government. The plaintiff at the time of filing the plaint described the suit property as follows : 

 "All that pieces and parcel of 3.79 three acres and seventy nine decimals of land in plot No. 148 khatian No. 88 mouza No. 8673 and mouza No. 626 Salia under PS Savar Dist. Dhaka." 

 14. At the time of filing the suit their case was that they were in possession of the suit land. But subsequently they came with the plea that during the pendency of the suit they have been dispossessed from the suit land and at their instance the prayer portion was amended by adding recovery of khas possession. When such an amendment is made the plaintiffs at the same-time ought to have prayed for amendment of the schedule of the land so that it may clearly indicate for which land they want recovery of khas possession. Subsequently the plaintiff filed a petition giving specific boundary from where they wanted to eject the defendants or, to say, recover their possession. In the case reported in 12 DLR page 626 the fact was that the application was for pre-emption by a co-sharer of the property transferred by kabala and what happened was that by some unfortunate error the property was described with reference to the Charcha Survey and not with reference to the CS Khatian. The court found that the Trial Court rightly allowed the amendment and decided the real question in dispute between the parties. The principle of law enunciated in that decision is that amendment may be allowed for giving specific description of the land for which the suit has been filed. In the present suit before us amendment was made describing clearly the land for which the plaintiff prayed for recovery of khas possession. In the case reported in 28 DLR 130 it has been held that where an amendment of the plaint in a suit does not alter the averment of the plaint but is sought in view of the subsequent happenings after the filing of the suit, such prayer for amendment can be allowed. Here in the present suit after filing of the suit the plaintiff made a prayer for recovery of possession alleging that during the pendency of the suit they have been dispossessed from the suit land. But while amending the plaint they failed to properly describe the land for which they prayed for recovery of khas possession. The present amendment in question has not changed the character and nature of the suit as the plaint has been amended making the present suit a suit for recovery of possession and also for declaration.
